hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
If this week is too heavy for a step, your task is honesty and one trusted believer. Tell God where you are. Tell one person.

Chapter 1 is careful here: holy waiting is real, and it's specific. If you're truly waiting on God for something only He can open, you're not failing. Read "Holy Waiting Is Real, and Specific" and let it steady you.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 1
read.body:
Open the book to Chapter 1, "Faith Is Not a Standstill." Read the opening, then two sections: "Screen Motion Is Not Obedience" and "I've Lived This Kind of Delay." Read the whole chapter if you can.

In the first section I name a quiet trap: feeds, threads, sermon clips, and saved videos that feel like movement while obedience stays frozen.

In the second, I tell you about Beaumont and Houston. I believed God was calling me to move, and then I kept adding conditions to a checklist and calling it wisdom. The finish line kept moving. Read it and ask if you've got a checklist like that.

Then come back here. And yes, I see the irony of sending you off your phone from inside an app. That's the point.

pulse.heading: The pulse: faith has feet
pulse.body:
Chapter 1 in one breath: biblical faith receives what God said and then responds in obedience. It rests on His character, and then it walks.

Abraham didn't get the map first. God spoke, and he went. His going wasn't the price of grace. It was the fruit of trusting the God who called him. Hebrews calls faith assurance and conviction, then spends a whole chapter on people whose belief got them moving.

pulse.quote: Biblical faith is not a spiritual parking brake.

verses.text: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father’s house to the land that I will show you.
So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

prompts: What did God say to Abram? What did Abram do?

nameIt.heading: Name it: the missing verb
nameIt.body:
Read these verses and circle the verbs in your head. Built. Went out. Crossed. Encircled. Faith in Hebrews 11 has feet.

Chapter 1 also honors waiting, so don't skip that part. Being still before God is real, and those who wait for the Lord renew their strength. But holy waiting is specific. The book gives five questions to test it. Here are three of them. Use them honestly. And be honest about your phone too.

bookRef.chapter: Chapter 1: Faith Is Not a Standstill
bookRef.section: Hebrews 11: Faith With Feet; Holy Waiting Is Real, and Specific

verses.text: By faith Noah, being warned by God concerning events as yet unseen, in reverent fear constructed an ark for the saving of his household. By this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith. By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going.

By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land, but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do the same, were drowned. By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.
“Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth!”
but they who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint.

prompts: Where have I used "I'm trusting God" to postpone a duty God already made plain?
Which faith verb is missing from my current "trust"?

Waiting check: Has God already made the next obedience clear in His Word? Would I wait this long if the cost of delay fell on someone I love? Have trusted believers confirmed this wait, or am I keeping it to myself?
Is my phone helping me obey, or helping me feel busy while I freeze?

build.heading: Build it: one step, not twenty plans
build.body:
Faith stands on God, and then it steps. Not twenty plans. One clear next step.

Chapter 1 also points out that clear doors are often already in front of us. Sometimes the door is a conversation, an application, a phone call, a gift you already have. Even our tools and platforms are talents to steward, not idols and not excuses.

Write one step you can finish in seven days. Give it a date. Name the one thing you'll stop, like the extra scroll or the next round of research. Name who you'll tell.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 1:

Name one clear next step, in one sentence. Do it within seven days. Tell one believer.

That's it. It's simple on purpose. If the date slips, don't throw the week away. Name the block, bring it to God, and set a new date within three days.

help.heading: Help: bring one answer, walk with one person
help.body:
Bring one answer from this stop to a trusted believer this week. The waiting check is a good one to share. Ask them straight: "Does this look like holy waiting to you, or delay?"

Then think of someone who's been in a long season of waiting. Don't preach at them, and don't decide for them whether their wait is holy. Ask how the waiting is going and how you can pray for them. Then listen.

pray.heading: Pray it
pray.body:
We don't look to our own grit. We look to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith. Pray this short and plain.

Lord Jesus, You started my faith and You'll finish it. I'm not leaning on my grit today. I'm leaning on You.

If I've been waiting on ____ when You already made ____ plain, forgive me for calling that faith.

Give me feet for one clear step: ____. I'll take it by ____. Help me as I go. Amen.

review.heading: Review: what faith is not
review.body:
After your date, come back and mark it honestly: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 1, "What Faith Is Not": faith isn't fear with Bible words on it. It isn't refusing the means God gives. It isn't calling Jesus Lord and not doing what He says. It isn't positive thinking. And it isn't sitting still with a verse attached.

And remember who grows the fruit. You plant and water. God gives the growth.

verses.text: “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I tell you?
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
